clauses.reason: The order exempts John M. Terwilliger, chief clerk, Office of the Collector of Internal Revenue, Detroit, Michigan, Treasury Department, from compulsory retirement for age under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, and fixes the period in its own words: "for a period of one year ending February 28, 1942". The recital says John M. Terwilliger had been exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year by Executive Order No. 8322 of January 15, 1940; those earlier orders precede this one and are not events of it. The end is recorded as February 28, 1942 (1942-02-28), inclusive: the exemption runs through that day. The exclusive reading, under which it ends when that day begins, is the alternative.

research_rationale:
EO 8690 is a one-person retirement exemption. Identity: the held text is the American Presidency Project page (node 368290, Common Crawl capture 2025-09-12T15:54:33Z); the page record with the same sha256 has a heading naming Executive Order 8690, the date 1941-02-19 that matches the signature date in the text, and a text_sha256 equal to the held file. The text was read in full: one recital paragraph, one operative sentence, signature and date. Inventory: a single clause, the exemption of John M. Terwilliger. End: the stated period gives 1942-02-28 as the first end by the order's own terms.  The packet's machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, OFR catalog, and held-text person-name search) record no hit that revokes, supersedes or shortens the order. The record rests on a transcription: original not yet held; replace and re-check quotes when an official copy is retrieved.

savings.reason: The order contains no sentence that operates after February 28, 1942 and no savings clause. Service that John M. Terwilliger rendered while the exemption was in force is a completed fact that the end of the period does not undo; that is the only effect that outlasts the order.
